FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
In work zones, move with the flow of traffic carefully and stay ready for sudden, unexpected events. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Speed limits may be lowered in work or construction zones and will be clearly posted; speeding there can bring double fines. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Speed is the biggest factor in how severe a crash is, and many deadly Colorado highway crashes involve drivers going too fast. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Posted speed limits are the most you may drive in ideal conditions; some roads like freeways also post a minimum, and going below it is a violation unless road or weather conditions require it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Slow down in poor weather and near railroad tracks, pedestrians, bicyclists, animals and school buses, but crawling far below the limit in normal conditions disrupts traffic flow and can be unsafe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Signs mark reduced speed zones, and you may need to go slower than any posted limit to keep everyone safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Unless signs say otherwise, blind curves and winding, narrow mountain highways carry a 20 mph Colorado limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
Unless signs say otherwise, the Colorado limit is 25 mph in a business district and 30 mph in a residence district. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
Unless signs say otherwise, the Colorado limit is 40 mph on open mountain highways and 45 mph for vehicles in the trash-hauling business. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Unless signs say otherwise, the Colorado limit is 55 mph on urban interstates and highways and 65 to 75 mph on designated rural interstates and highways; cities and towns may set lower limits by ordinance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
Stopping distance is how far you travel from the moment you realize you must stop until the vehicle stops, and it depends on speed, recognition time, reaction time and braking time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
Leaving space behind other vehicles lets you see stops coming, so slowing or changing lanes may avoid a stop or make it gradual and safer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
Sudden stops usually come from inattention or following too closely, and braking too hard can cause a skid, loss of control or a rear-end crash from the driver behind. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A01
The National Safety Council says a light passenger car at 55 mph can stop in roughly 200 feet under ideal conditions, while other vehicles need different distances. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A01
A proper turn means signaling early enough, scanning for hazards and crossing road users, turning from and into the correct lane on the correct path, then accelerating up to the limit or traffic flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A01
Not signaling is a traffic violation; signal before every turn, lane change, turn into a parking lot or pull-out from a parked spot so others know your intentions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A01
Before turning or changing lanes, keep signaling without a break for 100 feet in urban areas, or for 200 feet on four-lane highways posted above 40 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A01
A common rule of thumb is to signal for at least 3 seconds before turning or changing lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A01
If your turn signals fail you must use hand signals, ending the signal before the turn so both hands are on the wheel. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A01
For a right turn, start from the rightmost lane and turn from the right part of your lane as close to the curb as possible; for a left turn, keep to the left side of your lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A01
Where turns from more than one lane are allowed, signs, signals or lane markings will show the correct turn lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A01
End each turn centered in the proper lane of the road you enter, which is usually the closest lane on your side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A02
In intersections with several turn lanes, follow the white lines to find your path, and avoid cutting corners, swinging wide, turning late or straddling lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A02
Left turns are a frequent crash point; wait at the stop line or crosswalk until oncoming traffic leaves a gap big enough to finish the turn safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A02
Creeping into the intersection while waiting to turn left blocks emergency vehicles, cuts visibility for oncoming drivers and exposes you to red-light runners if the signal changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A02
Keep your front wheels pointed straight while waiting to turn left, because if you are hit from behind, turned wheels would push you into oncoming traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A02
A U-turn reverses your direction on the same road; it is banned where No U-turn signs are posted and anywhere it would endanger others, so go on to the next street or turnaround instead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A02
A two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction when driving around the block is not practical or possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A02
In a reverse two-point turnabout, signal right, check traffic, back until the rear bumper reaches the driveway edge, steer quickly full right while backing slowly, straighten once centered, then signal and turn left into the proper lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A02
In a forward two-point turnabout, signal left, pull in near the right side of the driveway or alley, stop once the rear clears the curb, signal right, reverse slowly with the wheel turned full right, straighten in the nearest lane, then drive forward. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A02
A three-point turnabout is only for a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn when there is no way around the block and no two-point option. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A02
For a three-point turnabout, pull over and stop on the right, then signal left at least 200 feet or three seconds ahead, check traffic and blind spots, and turn hard left to stop at the far side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A02
To finish a three-point turnabout, check both sides, reverse with the wheel turned sharply right across the road and stop, then in drive signal left, turn sharply left into the right lane of the new direction and check the signal has canceled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A02
When parking, leave an automatic in park; leave a manual in low gear facing uphill and in reverse facing downhill, set the emergency brake and take the key. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A02
Never park on a crosswalk, sidewalk, bridge, elevated structure, railroad tracks, controlled access highway, in an intersection, tunnel, runaway truck ramp, on or off ramp, in a bike lane, or across a driveway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A02
Parking is banned closer than 30 feet to a stop sign, traffic signal or railroad crossing, and closer than 15 feet to a fire hydrant. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A02
To parallel park, stop beside the car ahead, back slowly with the wheel sharp right, turn sharp left once clear of that car, then turn right to pull toward the curb in the middle of the space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A02
To leave a parallel space, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and pull out only when it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]
